gpt.rationale: For nonpayment of rent, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement only if the tenant fails to pay within seven calendar days after written notice of nonpayment and the landlord’s intent to terminate. Because eviction for possession follows termination of the rental agreement, this seven-day notice is required before filing.

gemini.rationale: The statute requires a landlord to deliver a written notice specifying the nonpayment of rent and stating the rental agreement will terminate not less than seven days after the tenant's receipt of the notice if the rent is not paid within that period.

federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.
federal.statute: 50 U.S.C. § 3951; as amended by Pub. L. 117-263, Div. E, Title LV, § 555 (FY23 NDAA, Dec. 23, 2022)
federal.threshold_formula: 130% of BAH for military member pay grade E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area in the United States (adjusted annually by DoD)

elements_confirmed: A material noncompliance by the landlord with the rental agreement or with the landlord's statutory duties to maintain the premises in a fit and habitable condition existed.
The tenant provided the landlord with a written notice specifying the acts and omissions constituting the breach.
The landlord failed to remedy the breach within fourteen days of receiving the written notice.
The condition was not caused by the deliberate or negligent act of the tenant or someone on the premises with the tenant's consent.
In an eviction action for nonpayment of rent, the tenant raises this issue as a counterclaim and may be ordered by the court to pay accrued rent into court.

substantive_defenses.note: Federal FHA prohibits discrimination in housing based on protected class. State law may provide additional protected classes and remedies. Discriminatory intent or disparate impact analysis is fact-intensive — specialist review required. grounding_gap: state fair housing case law and protected class details.

elements_confirmed: Tenant is a member of a protected class under the federal Fair Housing Act or the Nebraska Fair Housing Act (e.g., based on race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, or national origin).
Tenant was qualified to continue the tenancy (e.g., was complying with material lease terms).
Landlord initiated an eviction proceeding against the tenant.

The eviction was motivated by the tenant's membership in a protected class. This can be established through direct or circumstantial evidence, such as showing that similarly situated tenants who are not members of the protected class were not evicted.
